  enabled: false

[Open the construction notebook in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/quarcs-lab/geometrics/blob/main/notebooks/bolivia343_construction.ipynb) · [Notebook source](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/geometrics/blob/main/notebooks/bolivia343_construction.ipynb)

`geometrics.data.load_bolivia343()` returns **343 polygons and a 2012–2022
municipality/TIOC panel**. GDP is modeled and allocated by corrected grid
area. The default GDP per person now divides by **INE annual population
projections harmonized to map343**, not the gridded model population. This
is a denominator change, not a new survey or official municipal GDP. The same modern
geography is used for every year. It answers “how much of the gridded estimate
falls in today's footprint?” and does not imply every unit legally existed in
that year. `load_bolivia_harmonized("adm1")`, `load_bolivia_harmonized("adm2")` and
`load_bolivia_harmonized("adm3")` give the consistent levels on this backbone.
The older GADM loaders are retained for historical reproducibility.

## Inputs and units

| Input | Role |
|---|---|
| Rossi-Hansberg and Zhang, [Local GDP estimates around the world](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jue.2026.103871), via the [BFI Data Studio](https://bfidatastudio.org/gdp) | Model-estimated GDP and population on a 0.25° grid, 2012–2022. In the Bolivia `0_05` input, flagged low-density cells have zero estimated GDP, not necessarily zero population. |
| [Penn World Table 11.0](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/) | The existing geometrics GRID input is scaled by year to `rgdpo` (million 2021 US dollars at chained PPPs) and `pop` (million people). ADM3 redistributes these values geographically; it does not estimate new scaling factors. The GDP anchor is output-side real GDP at chained PPPs, not the `rgdpna` series based on national-accounts growth rates. |
| [INE Statistical Yearbook, table 2.01.12](https://anuario.ine.gob.bo/2023/documentos/201/20112.xlsx) | All-sex population projections, 2012–2022, used for the default per-capita denominator after a fixed-geography crosswalk. |
| [INE census counts, table 3.09.02.02](https://nimbus.ine.gob.bo/index.php/s/EgN8PPYD8Y4Rdig) | An exact 2012 census denominator for a separate ratio; counts from 2012 and 2024 also supply allocation shares for a small set of split units. |
| [SDSN Bolivia, Límites Municipales Bolivia 2025](https://sdsnbolivia.org/datos-espaciales/), accessed through the [GeoDevelopment Observatory of Bolivia](https://quarcs-lab.github.io/gdo4bolivia/) | Fixed 343-unit geography and Observatory IDs. The Observatory documents that it uses and shares this map with SDSN Bolivia's permission; the source is not represented as openly licensed. |

The GRID snapshot is pinned to geometrics commit
`c23a78de67db2a72c3243c43887927675b685c7c`; the
[municipal map](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/gdo4bolivia/blob/9a2e2b536b743700a69ca8b682ba57feb9bf7e26/geo/boundaries/map343.geojson)
is pinned to Observatory commit `9a2e2b536b743700a69ca8b682ba57feb9bf7e26`. The code checks the
expected hashes rather than trusting a moving branch or a replacement file
with the same name. This repository does not rehost the municipal map. Review
the source terms before redistributing municipal geometry (including derived
maps/geometry where applicable); the software license is not a data license.
The notebook builds to local runtime storage rather than uploading results.
The boundaries are statistical reference geography, not authority for legal
limits. See also the [official census portal's cartographic note](https://cpv2024.ine.gob.bo/).

## The grid origin was corrected

The [publisher's April 2026 data definitions](https://bfidatastudio.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Data-Definition.pdf)
specify the **southwest (bottom-left) corner**, not the center, for each
`longitude, latitude` pair. The original geometrics GRID polygons treated
those fields as centers, shifting their full squares 0.125° south and west.
The harmonized builder reconstructs each full square as
`[longitude, longitude + 0.25] × [latitude, latitude + 0.25]`; it does not
change the source GDP/population values or use census counts to choose an
offset. At international borders and large inland waters, the publisher's
actual source polygons may be clipped; this build reconstructs the full
envelopes, not those exact clipped shapes. Do not reuse the archived
legacy GeoPackage as corrected geometry.

## What the overlay does

The allocation uses **area overlap**, not the fraction of residents, lights
or firms known to be on each side of a boundary. For each grid cell, intersect
its polygon with the fixed municipal polygons in an equal-area coordinate
system (EPSG:6933). Ignore overlaps of 1 m² or less so a touch or a
numerical sliver does not count as support. Distribute its GDP and population to intersecting units in proportion
to their share of covered cell area. Denote intersection area by `a[i,j]`.
For a covered cell `i`, the conditional weights are
`w[i,j] = a[i,j] / sum_j(a[i,j])`. For each year, multiply each cell's
already anchored GDP and GRID population by these weights and sum by
municipal ID. Neither this sum nor the GDP/cell weights change when we
introduce the INE population denominator below. Never aggregate or allocate
precomputed GDP per capita or its logarithm.

The denominator is covered area, not the whole square. This conserves the
mass of **covered cells only**. Along borders it can allocate a whole estimate
from a small sliver of overlap. Cells with no qualifying overlap are left
unassigned and accounted for in the ledger, not snapped to a municipality or
redistributed. With these inputs, 6 of 1,603 cells are unassigned. The excluded
share is below **0.00017% of GDP** and **0.00014% of population** in every year.
Every municipality has support and the corrected grid envelopes cover
99.999% of the total municipal polygon area. That fraction measures geometry,
not residents or economic activity captured.

Two sensitivity runs change the grid allocation rule. Their population
totals and GDP-per-capita ratios use GRID population, not INE projections:

| 2022 allocation rule | GRID GDP unassigned | GRID population unassigned | Municipal GDP per capita available |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Covered-area share (main) | 0.000157% | 0.000117% | 343 |
| Full square denominator | 1.56% | 2.03% | 343 |
| Centroid, no nearest fallback | 1.37% | 1.75% | 277 |

For example, if A covers 25% of a cell and B 50%, the main method gives A
one-third and B two-thirds. The full-square method gives A one-quarter and B
one-half, leaving one-quarter unassigned. The centroid method assigns all of
a cell to the unit containing its center, or none if no unit contains it.
In 2022 GDP-per-capita rankings, full-square and main agree closely (Spearman
**0.996**), but the centroid comparison yields **0.886** on the 277 common
units. For 18 of those 277, centroid GDP per capita differs by more than 10%
from the main estimate. In Puerto Quijarro, for example, the full-square rule
changes GDP per capita from about **9,749** to **7,764** 2021 PPP US dollars. These are allocation
comparisons, not uncertainty bounds.

A small municipality may occupy only a fraction of one grid cell. An estimate
on that footprint does not provide independently observed within-cell detail.
Fixed polygons do not backcast legal history, area weights are no substitute
for a validated population/production surface, and the source's cell-level
tree quantiles cannot be summed into municipal uncertainty intervals.

## Which population belongs under GDP?

The annual INE yearbook covers **339 historical municipalities**. For
**333** modern units, a one-to-one roster match lets us use the annual
source projections as published. It does not establish identical historic
polygon edges. For the other **10** units, group the old municipalities
together where new units split from them. Pool the old municipalities'
published totals year by year, then divide each pool using the modern
units' within-group census shares. We interpolate those shares linearly
between 2012 and 2024 and convert to whole people without changing the
group total. Read `pop_ine_method` for `ine_yearbook_projection` (direct)
or `census_share_interpolated` (split). The latter is a retrospective
geographic harmonization,
not directly published INE municipal projections.

| Ratio | Denominator | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `gdppc` and `ln_gdppc` | `pop_ine`, INE projection in people | Default consistent annual series 2012–2022 |
| `gdppc_census_2012` | `pop_census_2012`, census count in people | Exact-year census denominator, 2012 only |
| `gdppc_pwt` and `ln_gdppc_pwt` | Original `pop_pwt`, GRID-modeled population in million people | Compare with the previous denominator |

All three ratios use the same GDP numerator. To divide by a population
in people, multiply `gdp_pwt` (millions of 2021 PPP US dollars) by
1 million first. GDP per capita is defined for positive populations;
logs are defined for positive ratios. Departments and provinces sum
the child GDP and population columns before calculating ratios. The
coarser estimates are rollups, not independent source publications, and
`n_population_split_units` identifies parents containing split units.
One linked Beni group crosses province boundaries.

The new 2012 annual projection differs from the census by **7.91%** at
the median municipality, versus **38.24%** for the corrected GRID population.
This is census agreement, not an independent holdout: [INE Revisión 2020,
§7(d)](https://siip.produccion.gob.bo/noticias/files/2021-934cb-1estimaINE.pdf#page=44) already uses the 2012 census to
adjust its municipal shares. The ten split estimates additionally use
census shares. [INE's newer municipal/TIOC series](https://www.ine.gob.bo/index.php/censos-y-proyecciones-de-poblacion-sociales/)
starts in 2024; its 2000–2050 national history does not replace the earlier
municipal series. The split is retrospective, using 2024 census
information; do not treat it as a contemporaneously available input to a
2012–2022 forecast or pre-treatment design.

This denominator switch does not move production. No building-surface
or gas-volume pilot weights are used by default. The ratio is still a
modeled measure and should not be used as official municipal GDP.

## Rebuild and inspect

Run the [notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/github/quarcs-lab/geometrics/blob/main/notebooks/bolivia343_construction.ipynb)
from the top, or in a geometrics clone run:

```bash
git rev-parse HEAD
uv run --locked --no-dev python tools/build_bolivia_adm3.py \
  --datasets-root datasets/BOL-005popAdj-PWTscaled \
  --output /tmp/geometrics-bolivia343
```

The Colab link on `main` is for discovery after merge. A notebook opened
from the implementation branch can use branch code before merge. Record
the full printed commit for your run and use it for an exact replay. The loader
constructs the result from pinned source files; it is not a download of a
premade municipal GDP file. An exact local copy of the municipal input can
be supplied via `--map343 /path/to/map343.geojson`; its checksum is still
verified. The build writes two panel CSVs: `bolivia_adm3_ine.csv` matches
the public loader, whereas `bolivia_adm3.csv` is the grid-only intermediate
whose `gdppc` still refers to modeled PWT population. Keep the intermediate
for grid-based validation below. The build also writes the local GeoPackage,
`allocation_ledger.csv`, `allocation_cell_weights.csv`, `sensitivity.csv` and
`validation.json` with the input hashes and geometry diagnostics.

```python
import geometrics as gm

gdf, df, dictionary = gm.data.load_bolivia343()
df = gm.set_labels(df, dictionary, set_panel=True)
gdf2, provinces, province_dictionary = gm.data.load_bolivia_harmonized("adm2")
```

## Three different checks

1. **Integrity:** Check the 343 IDs, the geometry-to-panel key set, the
   343 × 11 municipality-year grid, valid geometry and support, nonnegative
   additive totals, and GDP per capita defined only for positive population.
2. **Accounting:** Re-sum municipal GDP and **GRID** population by year and
   compare with the original GRID totals less the disclosed unassigned
   residual. Separately check that the **INE** denominator sums to the
   original INE projection totals. The two population concepts do not have
   to match. Neither check validates municipal GDP.
3. **External checks and sensitivity:** Compare 2022 model departmental GDP
   shares with [INE departmental accounts, table D.10.1.2](https://www.ine.gob.bo/referencia2017/pib_departamental.html);
   this is an independent sanity check on broad spatial patterns, not a
   like-for-like validation of PPP real GDP (INE's comparison table is in
   current prices) or municipal accuracy. The [INE census
   tables](https://www.ine.gob.bo/index.php/estadisticas-sociales/poblacion-censo/)
   benchmark the previous GRID population in 2012. They did not select the
   corrected area-GDP allocation. The 2012 census informs both the underlying
   INE projections and the new population splits; 2024 counts also inform
   the splits. Neither endpoint is a held-out test of those estimates. Do not infer
   that the upstream LandScan product is independent of all census information.

In the optional 2022 benchmark, Santa Cruz accounts for **24.39%** of the
model's municipal GDP when aggregated to departments, versus **32.23%** in
the INE nominal accounts. La Paz goes the other way (**32.69%** vs **26.17%**).
Cochabamba's shares are **20.08%** and **15.08%**, respectively. Across nine
departments, the rank correlation is **0.97**, with a mean absolute share
difference of **2.64 percentage points**. INE marks 2022 preliminary. These
differences are visible even at department scale, and can reflect both the
underlying model and differing price concepts. They do not establish how
accurately the 0.25° cells distribute GDP within small municipalities.


The GDP numerator still has substantial uncertainty. In a separate official
departmental volume check for 2017–2022, the modeled and INE cumulative
GDP growth ranks correlated **0.383**. In 2019 the corrected area numerator
and FAM–AR-LAT GDP estimates, divided by the same INE population and
coarsened to 337 common municipal groups, had rank agreement of **0.214**.
FAM is another model, not municipal accounts. These checks do not establish
which estimate is more accurate. The population improvement should not be
read as a validation of the GDP numerator.


## Why retain the previous population denominator as a diagnostic?

The [pinned geo4bolivia/GDO SDG population series](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/gdo4bolivia/blob/9a2e2b536b743700a69ca8b682ba57feb9bf7e26/docs/datasets/sdg.md)
uses the same map343 geography. Its 2012 counts, including four footprints
created as administrative units later, match all 343 municipal/TIOC records
in [INE table 3.09.02.02](https://nimbus.ine.gob.bo/index.php/s/EgN8PPYD8Y4Rdig)
after matching nested names and verifying the GDO keys. GDO parent crosswalks
give 113 provinces and nine departments. The 2024 census is outside the GDP
panel and is not a 2022 observation; the GDO and INE 2024 Huarina values differ
(8,279 vs 8,679).

| Scale | Units | Population rank correlation: old → corrected | Median absolute percentage error: old → corrected |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Municipal / TIOC | 343 | 0.649 → 0.822 | 54.05% → 38.24% |
| Province | 113 | 0.787 → 0.944 | 46.22% → 19.54% |
| Department | 9 | 0.983 → 1.000 | 9.29% → 4.94% |

For GRID population, the coordinate correction markedly improves spatial
agreement, but **227 of 343** municipal populations remain more than 25%
away from the census.
For example, the corrected counts are about **856,422** for Santa Cruz de la
Sierra and **428,031** for adjacent La Guardia, versus **1,444,425** and
**89,284** in INE. The corrected national aggregate is **10.52 million**
versus **10.06 million** observed, consistent with different population
anchors. Municipal coverage, a balanced accounting ledger and a good
department rank correlation do not make municipal GDP per capita reliable.

Reproduce with the notebook or the separate script. The script reads the
pinned GDO and INE files, checks their hashes and writes local benchmark
tables without publishing the geometry:

```bash
uv run --locked --with openpyxl python tools/validate_bolivia_census.py \
  --adm3 /tmp/geometrics-bolivia343/bolivia_adm3.csv \
  --out /tmp/geometrics-bolivia343-census
```

For the named projection groups see the [ADM3 construction record](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/geometrics/blob/main/datasets/BOL-005popAdj-PWTscaled/ADM3/README.md).
